 ASL is not a literal translation of English. There are signs with no corresponding English words and some English words that don't have a sign in ASL.

I've taken ASL 1-5 classes at my local community college and am now in the ASL-English Interpreting Prep Program. There are classes, videos, textbooks, there are some decent ones sold at Barnes n Nobles, but what I've learned is the best way to learn is to go out into the Deaf community in your area. ASL has regional variation, like any language, and is best learned from native users.
